xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2500: memory-aware resource governor — autonomous resume/dispatch bypasses the RAM admission gate the HTTP spawn path enforces (OOM root cause)

plan.title: feat(cloister): memory-aware resource governor — autonomous resume/dispatch bypasses the RAM admission gate the HTTP spawn path enforces (OOM root cause)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: Two admission gates exist and disagree. The HTTP spawn path (operator Start / CLI pan start) is memory-aware: evaluateSpawnGuardrails (src/dashboard/server/routes/agents/shared.ts:557) blocks with 429 when MemAvailable is below the critical threshold. The deacon's autonomous resume/dispatch path (autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents, applyBootReconciliationDecision, handleAgentStoppedEvent in src/lib/cloister/deacon-auto-resume.ts) never calls that gate — it admits on work-agent count (max_work_agents=6) and 1-minute CPU load only. `git grep evaluateSpawnGuardrails src/lib/cloister` returns nothing. Because the count never sees each workspace's multi-GB docker stack, the deacon resuming orphaned agents on boot exhausts RAM and systemd-oomd kills the whole tmux server (#2390). `pan up --no-resume` is the only existing escape.
narratives.Proposal: Give the deacon a memory-aware, hysteresis-guarded admission control loop that consumes the same MemAvailable signal and the #2464 per-stack RSS attribution. (1) Extract the memory-pressure predicate into ONE shared function both doors call. (2) Add SOFT/HARD/RECOVERY hysteresis bands (recovery>soft) so it can't oscillate. (3) Admit on estimated footprint in bytes (claude RSS + supervisor + workspace docker-stack RSS + tool-spike reserve), learned from live docker stats. (4) Under HARD pressure shed cheapest-value-first (docker stop merged/closed stacks -> pause idle work agents; never docker pause for RAM). (5) Shrink the reserved advancing-slot budget under pressure. (6) Replace the boot grace->resume_all burst with a memory-paced trickle. (7) Set ManagedOOMPreference=avoid on the tmux-server unit so a governor miss degrades gracefully.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do NOT change the HTTP spawn path's operator-facing behavior (429 semantics, thresholds) beyond routing it through the shared predicate.
- Do NOT introduce a second/forked set of memory thresholds — one source of truth only.
- Do NOT use `docker pause` to reclaim RAM (it retains RSS; only frees CPU).
- Do NOT shed operator-attached agents or core services (dashboard, deacon, cliproxy, traefik).
- Do NOT change the count-based concurrency caps (max_work_agents / reserved_advancing_slots / reserved_swarm_slots) when RAM is plentiful.
- Do NOT change DEFAULT_BOOT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_SECS; only the apply-loop becomes memory-governed.
- Do NOT rebuild #2464's observability/manual controls — reuse them.
- No new synchronous/blocking calls in server-reachable code.

autoDecisions.summary: Place the new SOFT/HARD/RECOVERY band-reserve config in config-yaml `resources` (alongside existing memoryWarnGb/memoryBlockGb at src/lib/config-yaml/defaults.ts:176-177), NOT in cloister/config.ts as PRD W2 loosely suggested.
autoDecisions.rationale: The memory admission thresholds evaluateSpawnGuardrails already gates on are sourced from config-yaml resources and consumed at system-health-service.ts:257-258. Co-locating the governor bands there keeps one memory-admission tuning surface and lets the shared predicate read one threshold object (single-source-of-truth). cloister.toml holds count/load concurrency, a different axis.

autoDecisions.summary: Default band reserves expressed as a fraction of totalmem() with an absolute floor: SOFT=max(15% total, 8GB), HARD=max(8% total, 4GB), RECOVERY=max(25% total, 12GB); cold-start per-role footprint default configured explicitly.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD W2's implementation checkpoint offered this exact fallback when host-specific numbers are unclear; fraction+floor generalizes off the 62GB incident box without a hardcoded literal (NFR-3).

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD W1 into two beads: mem-governor-module (module + shared predicate refactor) and wire-deacon-gate (the three deacon call sites).
autoDecisions.rationale: Each is independently reviewable and mergeable; the module refactor is behavior-preserving and the wiring bead is the standalone OOM fix. Foundation status (inspection) attaches cleanly to the module bead.

items.title: Create memory-governor.ts with assessMemoryPressure() and a shared memory-pressure predicate

expected_outputs: memory-governor.test.ts passes with assessMemoryPressure returning ok/soft/hard at the configured boundaries
metadata.readinessReason: Root foundation with no upstream dependency; it is the sole first edit to the new memory-governor.ts module and the behavior-preserving evaluateSpawnGuardrails refactor, so nothing else races it.

narrative.Action: Create src/lib/cloister/memory-governor.ts exporting `assessMemoryPressure(): Promise<MemoryVerdict>` where MemoryVerdict = { band: 'ok'|'soft'|'hard', availableBytes: number, thresholds }. Read MemAvailable via the existing async parser readProcMemory() (system-health-service.ts:332 -> readProcMemoryLinux():268, MemAvailable at :279) — do NOT add a new /proc reader. Extract the memory-pressure comparison currently inline in evaluateSpawnGuardrails (shared.ts:557-569) into a single shared predicate (e.g. classifyMemoryPressure(availableBytes, thresholds)) exported from memory-governor.ts (or a small shared module), and refactor evaluateSpawnGuardrails to call it so both doors share ONE implementation. This bead is behavior-preserving for the HTTP path. All I/O async (NFR-1). Bands beyond ok/soft/hard are added in hysteresis-bands; this bead may treat 'critical threshold crossed' as hard and 'warning threshold crossed' as soft using the existing memoryAvailableCriticalBytes/memoryAvailableWarningBytes.

items.title: assessMemoryPressure() returns band 'hard' when MemAvailable is below the critical threshold, 'soft' when below the warning threshold, and 'ok' otherwise (verified with a stubbed readProcMemory)

evaluateSpawnGuardrails(shared.ts) calls the extracted shared predicate rather than an inline comparison; `git grep classifyMemoryPressure src/dashboard/server/routes/agents/shared.ts` returns a match and existing spawn-guardrail behavior is preserved (429 on critical)

The module reads MemAvailable exclusively through the async readProcMemory path (no execSync, no new synchronous /proc read); memory-governor.test.ts passes when driving the boundaries with a stubbed snapshot
Wire assessMemoryPressure() into the three deacon resume/dispatch call sites (core OOM fix)

expected_outputs: deacon-resume test with assessMemoryPressure stubbed to 'soft' asserts zero resumes and a memory-gate deferral log

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/deacon-auto-resume.ts add an `await assessMemoryPressure()` gate immediately beside each existing load gate: (1) the autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents loop (load gate at :853-855), (2) the applyBootReconciliationDecision loop (load gate at :927-929), (3) the handleAgentStoppedEvent global-gate block (load gate at :751-754). When band !== 'ok', mirror the load gate's defer-not-kill behavior exactly: logDeaconEventSync with a memory-gate message including availMB, then break (loops) / return null (handleAgentStoppedEvent). Never kill or shed here — deferral only (that is FR-6's job).

items.title: With assessMemoryPressure stubbed to band 'soft', autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents resumes zero agents and emits a logDeaconEventSync line naming the memory gate and observed availMB
applyBootReconciliationDecision and reactive handleAgentStoppedEvent each defer (resume zero) when band is 'soft' or 'hard', leaving candidate state untouched for the next patrol
`git grep -l assessMemoryPressure src/lib/cloister/deacon-auto-resume.ts` shows the gate present, and all three call sites appear (AC-1 of PRD)
When band is 'ok' the resume/dispatch behavior is unchanged from before this bead (count + load gates still apply, agents resume as before)
Add SOFT/HARD/RECOVERY hysteresis bands and the governor shed/recover state machine

expected_outputs: hysteresis test asserts no re-admit between SOFT and RECOVERY

narrative.Action: Add three config-driven reserve thresholds to config-yaml `resources` (schema.ts, defaults.ts, merge.ts) alongside the existing memoryWarnGb/memoryBlockGb: governorSoftReserveGb, governorHardReserveGb, governorRecoveryReserveGb (RECOVERY strictly > SOFT). Defaults as fractions of totalmem() with floors: SOFT=max(15% total, 8GB), HARD=max(8% total, 4GB), RECOVERY=max(25% total, 12GB). No hardcoded silent fallback (NFR-3). In memory-governor.ts hold a tiny state machine { mode: 'admitting'|'holding'|'shedding' } that transitions ONLY on band crossings, and does not re-admit until MemAvailable exceeds RECOVERY. assessMemoryPressure now derives band from these bands. Any delay-based test uses fake timers.

items.title: Given a MemAvailable sequence that crosses SOFT downward then rises just past SOFT but below RECOVERY, the governor stays in 'holding' and re-admits nothing until MemAvailable exceeds RECOVERY

The three reserve thresholds resolve from config-yaml resources; an unset value falls back to the documented fraction-of-totalmem default (not a silent code literal), and RECOVERY is rejected/normalized if not strictly greater than SOFT
With a threshold-straddling workload, assessMemoryPressure produces a stable mode across successive calls (no admitting<->shedding oscillation) within the test window
Gigabyte-budget admission: estimateFootprint() with docker-stack accounting

expected_outputs: footprint admission test defers the N+1th agent whose summed footprint exceeds the free budget
metadata.readinessReason: Serialized onto the shared memory-governor.ts module by blocks edges from mem-governor-module and hysteresis-bands, so it never edits that file concurrently with another bead; dispatchable alone once unblocked.

narrative.Action: Extend memory-governor.ts with `estimateFootprint(role, projectKey): Promise<number>` sourced from live per-stack RSS (reuse DockerStatsCollector in src/lib/docker-stats.ts and sumProcessMemory at system-health-service.ts:421 — the #2464 attribution) plus an explicit configured cold-start default per role (config-yaml resources; no silent literal). Export an admission predicate `canAdmit(footprint, availableBytes): boolean` = footprint <= availableBytes - softReserve. All docker stats reads async (NFR-1). This is the shared estimator the specialist-budget, tiered-eviction, and memory-paced-boot beads consume — pin its public shape here.

items.title: canAdmit defers an agent whose estimated footprint would exceed MemAvailable minus the SOFT reserve, even when a count slot is free (PRD AC-3)
estimateFootprint returns a learned per-stack value from a stubbed docker stats map when available, and falls back to the configured cold-start default per role otherwise
Admission accepts N agents whose summed estimated footprint fits the free budget and defers the N+1th (verified with a stubbed budget)
All docker-stats/proc reads in the estimator are async (no execSync); the cold-start footprint default resolves from config, not an inline literal
On-demand specialist budget: shrink reserved advancing slots under pressure

expected_outputs: advancing-dispatch test withholds under SOFT despite a free count slot

narrative.Action: Where advancing dispatch is gated (canDispatchAdvancing at src/lib/cloister/concurrency.ts:160, and tryReserveAdvancingSlot / its callers), add a footprint/band check so a review/test specialist is spawned only when advancing work exists AND footprint budget exists (canAdmit true and band==='ok'). Do NOT change the reserved-slot count semantics when RAM is plentiful (band==='ok' -> existing behavior unchanged).

items.title: Advancing dispatch is withheld when band==='soft' even though a count slot is free (PRD AC-5)
Advancing dispatch proceeds normally when band==='ok' and footprint budget exists — count-slot semantics unchanged under plentiful RAM
A specialist is admitted only when there is actual advancing work AND canAdmit returns true (no reserving GB for a slot with nothing to advance)
Tiered eviction under HARD pressure: stop merged stacks, then pause idle agents

expected_outputs: shed test stops merged stacks before pausing an agent and never sheds an operator-attached agent
metadata.readinessReason: Serialized onto the shared memory-governor.ts module by blocks edges from footprint-budget and hysteresis-bands, so it never edits that file concurrently with another bead; dispatchable alone once unblocked.

narrative.Action: Add `shed(target): Promise<ShedResult>` to memory-governor.ts, invoked when band==='hard', reclaiming in value-ascending order until MemAvailable clears RECOVERY or nothing shed-eligible remains: (1) docker stop stacks whose issue is merged/closed — reuse buildReclaimPayload + isClosedStack (stack.phase==='merged') from src/dashboard/server/routes/resources/reclaim.ts; do NOT re-derive 'safe to stop'. (2) pause idle work agents (runtime.state==='idle') via setAgentPaused (src/lib/agents/agent-state.ts:423) with a pausedReason marking a governor shed so recovery/pan-unpause clears it — this frees the claude RSS and the agent resumes via --resume when RECOVERY is crossed. NEVER shed an operator-attached agent or a core service (dashboard/deacon/cliproxy/traefik). NEVER docker pause to reclaim RAM. All docker calls async (NFR-1).

items.title: With two merged-issue stacks and one idle work agent under HARD pressure, shed stops both stacks first then pauses the agent only if still under HARD after the stacks (PRD AC-4)
shed refuses to select an operator-attached agent or a core service, and never issues `docker pause` to reclaim RAM (only `docker stop`)

Pausing an idle agent preserves its tmux session and workspace and records a pausedReason identifying the governor shed, so recovery/pan-unpause clears it and the agent resumes via the normal --resume path once RECOVERY is crossed
shed applies reclaim.ts's merged/closed determination (isClosedStack / buildReclaimPayload) rather than a re-derived safe-to-stop computation
Memory-paced boot: replace grace->resume_all burst with a governed trickle

expected_outputs: boot-trickle test resumes only as many as fit the budget and defers the rest with the memory reason

narrative.Action: In applyBootReconciliationDecision (deacon-auto-resume.ts:885, apply-loop from :917) change the candidate loop so that after each resume it awaits a short RSS-settle window then re-runs assessMemoryPressure()/estimateFootprint before admitting the next candidate; on band!=='ok' break and leave remaining candidates deferred for the next memory-governed patrol. Keep the existing per-agent skip/deferred bookkeeping and the existing RESUME_STAGGER_MS staggering. Do NOT change DEFAULT_BOOT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_SECS (boot-reconciliation.ts:19). Tests use fake timers for the settle window.

items.title: Boot with 20 candidates and a MemAvailable that drops below SOFT after 3 resumes: the apply-loop accepts exactly 3 and defers 17 with the memory reason — not a resume_all burst (PRD AC-6)
The apply-loop re-checks assessMemoryPressure between each admit (settle window driven by fake timers) and preserves existing per-agent skip/deferred bookkeeping
When MemAvailable never clears, remaining candidates are deferred (recorded) for the next patrol and the loop exits without spinning
Kernel safety net: set ManagedOOMPreference=avoid on the tmux-server unit

expected_outputs: systemctl show overdeck-tmux-server.service -p ManagedOOMPreference reports avoid after a founding

narrative.Action: In src/lib/tmux.ts add '--property=ManagedOOMPreference=avoid' to the systemd-run args that found the managed tmux server (currently at :299: ['--user','--unit',MANAGED_TMUX_SERVER_UNIT,'--collect','--quiet','--service-type=forking','tmux',...args]). This deprioritizes the tmux server for systemd-oomd so a governor miss degrades gracefully instead of wiping all agent processes at once (#2390). This is the tmux founding primitive (pre-server) — the existing execFileSync there is legitimate; no new sync call is introduced and no-execSync-server is not violated. The non-systemd fallback branch is unaffected.

items.title: The systemd-run founding args contain --property=ManagedOOMPreference=avoid; after a founding, `systemctl show overdeck-tmux-server.service -p ManagedOOMPreference` shows `avoid` (PRD AC-7)
The change adds only the property arg — the non-systemd (setsid/plain) fallback branch and existing founding behavior are otherwise unchanged and typecheck passes
